findings: High: The current composition does not place the illustrative example on each model node. `renderExamples()` builds a separate subtype-level example strip from synthetic templates in `SUBTYPE_EXAMPLES`, while architecture cards show only a selected figure plus a short route preview. That can let users read the example as model-specific evidence even though it is detached from the node and not paper-derived. recommended_graph: Make the primary landing view a graph: family nodes at the top, subtype nodes beneath them, and model nodes as the leaves. Keep the current catalog as a secondary drill-down, not the default framing.

Render each model node as a split tile: left side = original-paper evidence image, right side = illustrative input example. Label them explicitly as "Evidence" and "Illustrative example" so the viewer cannot confuse source imagery with explanatory scaffolding.

Use different visual grammar for the two sides. Evidence should use a paper-artifact frame with figure number, page, DOI/record, and SHA-256 badge. The example should use a code/sample style with no provenance fields.

Show per-route certainty in-band with badges for `explicit_text`, `text_plus_figure`, `inferred`, plus `input_status` and `final_grounding_valid`. Do not default-inflate all routes to the same confidence level.

For multi-route models, aggregate by model node but allow the detail drawer to fan out into route-level evidence rows; preserve explicit arrows for source object → transformation chain → model-visible carrier.
risks: The current subtype examples are synthetic templates, so they can be mistaken for paper-derived inputs unless the UI marks them as illustrative-only.
A single selected figure may overrepresent models with heterogeneous routes unless the detail view lets users inspect all route-specific evidence.
Without explicit crop metadata, "crop from original paper figure" remains an upstream assumption; the build can only faithfully reuse what the corpus provides.
acceptance_checks: Every model node displays exactly one evidence artifact and one illustrative input example in the same panel or modal, with separate headings and styling.
Evidence artifacts always show paper title, figure index, page, record/DOI, and SHA-256; illustrative examples never show provenance metadata.
Routes with `evidence_status != explicit_text` are visibly flagged and excluded from the default high-confidence rendering.
The landing view renders explicit taxonomy edges (`family → subtype → model`) and not just grouped lanes or a catalog list.
The build fails, or labels clearly, if a model lacks a figure crop/panel, if a route lacks grounded evidence, or if the example is not tied to the subtype/model context.
